subject: Post-call recap — SparrowPay pilot economics & budget commitment criteria
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@sparrowpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — SparrowPay pilot economics & budget commitment criteria

Hi Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain & goals (from your side)
- Unpredictable inference spend month-to-month; dev team sees big variance tied to peak campaigns.
- Need predictable cost envelope for launch (Q3) — target is to keep inference run-rate under $12k/month for 2M monthly API calls (avg prompt ~90 tokens, gen ~150 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 400ms for short prompts; tolerance for occasional spikes during peak auth checks.
- Security: must run through our hosted offering with data isolation controls and audit logs; SOC2 evidence requested.

What we propose for the pilot (3 weeks active, sandbox + traffic replay)
- Objective: validate expected unit economics with production-like traffic and confirm levers to hit your budget cap.
- Scope: 50k daily requests replayed (representative mix), initial model: LlamaX-13B-quant (we can bump down to 7B for staging).
- Primary levers to test: continuous batching (reduces per-token infra by ~15–30% depending on request shape), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (expected reduction in generated tokens 20–60% on your conversational flows), and int8 quantization to reduce GPU footprint.
- Success criteria: measured net cost-per-1k output tokens <= $0.90 (end-to-end, after batching/caching) OR meet your <$12k/month projection when scaled to 2M calls.

Numbers we discussed (your inputs + initial Redwood model)
- Current estimate you shared: ~2M calls / month, ~240M gen tokens/month.
- Rough Redwood baseline (no batching/cache): ~ $2.5k–$3.2k per 100M tokens (varies by model/shape).
- Pilot target (with batching + caching): 30–55% reduction on the per-token billable usage compared to the naive baseline.

Asks from SparrowPay (what we need to run the pilot)
1) An anonymized 48-hour traffic dump (JSON) or production sampling endpoint; PII redacted.
2) A point contact in procurement for a short pilot agreement / PO (we can run on a short-term order).
3) SRE/infra contact to set up IP allowlist and any VPC peering requirements.
4) Confirmation on which data retention window you require for logs/usage metrics.

Next steps & timeline
- Fri 6/14: Redwood to send pilot statement-of-work + estimated cost workbook (attached).
- Mon 6/16: SparrowPay to share traffic sample + procurement contact.
- Week of 6/23: Kickoff (environment + replay), run 3 active weeks, deliver cost report and ops playbook.

Attached: starter pilot TCO workbook and our pricing anchor. I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link for an MSA amendment to cover the pilot.

Thanks again — excited to help SparrowPay get a predictable inference footprint.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: SparrowPay_Pilot_TCO_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Pricing_anchors.pdf

From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@sparrowpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SparrowPay pilot economics & budget commitment criteria

Thanks for the clear summary, Rafael — this matches our notes. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

1) The 2M calls/month number is a steady-state projection; our immediate 6–8 week ramp may see spikes up to 3.5–4M/day during marketing promos (we'll mark those as out-of-scope for the pilot).
2) For the traffic sample we can provide a 72-hour scrubbed dataset (will remove emails and card identifiers). Can you confirm preferred schema? JSON lines with timestamp, session id, prompt, response-length?
3) Procurement: loop in procurement@sparrowpay.com; they generally need a pilot SOW + short PO; target turn is 10 business days.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you include an alternate scenario that uses a smaller model (7B quant) and an estimate of any quality delta? We need to understand QoE risk vs cost.
- Can Redwood guarantee a fallback policy so that if latency > 700ms we route to a lower-cost model automatically?

We expect to name a PO approver this week and get the data sample over by Monday.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Wu
Head of ML Product, SparrowPay
alex.wu@sparrowpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SparrowPay pilot economics & budget commitment criteria

Looping in for SRE + sales ops alignment. Rafael — I’ll own the SOW and procurement pack, Karthik can scope the model/quantization tradeoffs for the 7B vs 13B scenario.

Action items I’ll pick up:
- Draft short pilot SOW and send to Alex by EOD Friday (6/14).
- Populate the pricing workbook with a conservative and aggressive scenario (batching on/off + prefix cache on/off).
- Request SOC2 summary and audit evidence for their security team.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: 2027-06-14T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SparrowPay pilot economics & budget commitment criteria

Great — thanks Alex + Marissa. Confirming we will: 
- Send SOW + pricing workbook by EOD Friday (6/14). DocuSign link will be included: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/Envelope/ABC-123-PILOT
- Pilot kickoff timeline: environment setup week of 6/23.
- Karthik will run a comparative quality check (7B quant vs 13B quant) and include estimated token/cost deltas.
- Security package (SOC2 summary, retention options) attached to SOW.

For the traffic sample schema Alex — please send JSONL with these fields: timestamp, session_id, prompt_text, response_length, user_type. If you prefer, we can provide a small ingestion script to map your export.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/3421 (I added the SOW and pricing workbook as attachments).

If procurement can provision the PO contact, we’ll slot a pilot order and provide the IP allowlist details. 

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—Rafael
